elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend.
elements.evidence: The added language states that “TrueLink shall defend” Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to indemnify.
elements.evidence: The added language states that “TrueLink shall ... indemnify” Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Customer and Customer’s affiliates are protected beneficiaries of the Vendor indemnity.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly protects “Client and its affiliates.”

elements.element: The specified Vendor indemnity applies to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The added language applies to “any third-party claim” and grammatically extends that limitation to each listed claim category.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause covers claims alleging that “the Hosting Services or any deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies against third-party claims arising from Vendor’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly covers claims arising out of “TrueLink’s breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause covers claims arising from “any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content caused by TrueLink,” which operatively addresses a TrueLink-caused data breach.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies against third-party claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly covers claims arising from “TrueLink’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.”

elements.element: Customer must provide notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Client to give TrueLink “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: Vendor has control of the defense of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that “TrueLink has control of the defense.”

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.
elements.evidence: The clause requires that “Client provides reasonable cooperation.”

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Paragraph a(iii) covers claims arising out of or relating to “Client Content,” including content posted by Client and its personnel.

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for claims arising from Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: Paragraph a(ii) refers only to acts or omissions constituting “a violation of any state or federal law” within a broader and grammatically ambiguous System Agreement/Credit Repository Agreement trigger. It does not clearly cover Customer’s breach of all applicable law as a standalone basis.

elements.element: Customer has no indemnity obligations beyond claims arising from Customer-provided content and Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: Customer’s indemnity remains substantially broader, including any breach of the Agreement, acts by Client customers causing TrueLink defaults or loss of contractual rights, claims relating generally to the Web Site, and injury or property damage from products, services, or information distributed through the Web Site.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims involving the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: The added clause indemnifies Client against third-party claims alleging that the Hosting Services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual-property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Customer appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement resulting from Customer specifications or instructions.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Customer specifications or instructions appears in the operative language.

elements.element: As an IP-infringement remedy, Vendor must procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no obligation to procure continued usage rights.

elements.element: As an IP-infringement remedy, Vendor must modify the affected services or deliverables to be noninfringing.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: As an IP-infringement remedy, Vendor must replace the affected services or deliverables with a noninfringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: As an IP-infringement remedy, Vendor must provide a refund if the other remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or 3× annual-fees super-cap appears in the operative language.

result.reason: The added operative sentence substantially supplies the preferred Vendor-side indemnity and procedure, but the existing Customer indemnity remains far broader than the permitted content-and-law scope and does not clearly state a standalone indemnity for all Customer breaches of applicable law. The fallback is also incomplete because it lacks all stated IP exclusions, infringement remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. The addition is generally coherent and does not contradict the existing Vendor indemnity, but it does not reach either complete position and is awkwardly appended without the separately labeled subparagraph described in the non-operative comment.
